note: adversarial verification of the E1 verdicts (independent agents; tracer-free GOT probes and ud2 trap matrix; tooling review). Poisoned .so copies are not kept.

results.claim: (B) untagged co-loaded: the later-loaded artifact's calls run the FIRST-loaded artifact's compute code, whatever the call order. Also checked: whether gdb/ptrace or LD_DEBUG could have produced this, and whether the entry itself could have come from the wrong DSO.
independent_checks: Static ELF (readelf -rW / objdump). Both files are named model.so, have no SONAME and export the same names: run_main_graph_model, _mlir_ciface_main_graph_model and main_graph_model. S8 JUMP_SLOTs: _mlir_ciface at GOT 0x9098 and main_graph at 0x9078. S1 JUMP_SLOTs: 0xa098 and 0xa078. In both files the PLT stubs are at 0x2160 (ciface) and 0x2120 (main_graph), and each stub is a plain `jmp *GOT`. run_main_graph_model calls _mlir_ciface_main_graph_model@plt (S8 at 0x30f3, S1 at 0x3b73). _mlir_ciface calls main_graph_model@plt (S8 at 0x2fa4, S1 at 0x3a24). Symbol values: S8 entry 0x2ff0, ciface 0x2f90, main 0x23b0 (size 3026); S1 entry 0x3a70, ciface 0x3a10, main 0x23b0 (size 5728). The on-disk sha256 values still match the claimed ones (6e8faed1... and 01328b45...).

Runtime source at pinned 1e017c9f, src/Runtime/ExecutionSession.cpp: dlopen(path, RTLD_LAZY|RTLD_GLOBAL) at line 132, then setEntryPoint("run_main_graph"+lowDashTag) using dlsym(_sharedLibraryHandle, ...) at line 247.

Tracer-free GOT probe (scratchpad/e1_verify/B_tracerfree/got_probe.py). Each run is a plain python process with TracerPid=0 in /proc/self/status and no LD_* variables (a separate set of runs uses LD_BIND_NOW=1 only). The load base comes from dl_iterate_phdr. The 8-byte GOT slot is read with ctypes. Each slot value is mapped to a DSO by both dladdr and /proc/self/maps, and the two always agreed. Twelve runs in total: isolated S8, isolated S1, and four co-load orders, each in lazy and bind-now mode.

LAZY, load S8 then S1, call S1 first (pid 32660; S8 base 0x7fc5d5286000, S1 base 0x7fc5d4885000). After the call: S1 GOT[0xa098]@0x7fc5d488f098 = 0x7fc5d5288f90, which dladdr gives as S8:_mlir_ciface_main_graph_model (S8+0x2f90). S1 GOT[0xa078] still holds 0x7fc5d4887126, S1's unresolved lazy stub (base+0x2126). S8 GOT[0x9078] = 0x7fc5d52883b0, S8:main_graph_model (S8+0x23b0). S8 GOT[0x9098] still holds 0x7fc5d5288166 (unresolved), so S8's entry did not run. Output was an exact permutation. The later S8 and S1 calls leave S1 GOT[0xa098] pointing at S8+0x2f90.

LAZY, load S8 then S1, call S8 first (pid 32670; S8 base 0x7f097bf20000, S1 base 0x7f097a685000). After calling S8, both S1 slots are still unresolved. After calling S1: S1 GOT[0xa098] = 0x7f097bf22f90, which is S8+0x2f90. S1 GOT[0xa078] is still unresolved (0x7f097a687126).

LAZY, load S1 then S8, call S8 first (pid 32680; S1 base 0x7f4209885000, S8 base 0x7f4208e86000). After the call: S8 GOT[0x9098]@0x7f4208e8f098 = 0x7f4209888a10, which is S1:_mlir_ciface (S1+0x3a10). S8 GOT[0x9078] is still unresolved (0x7f4208e88126). S1 GOT[0xa078] = 0x7f42098873b0, S1:main_graph_model (S1+0x23b0). S1 GOT[0xa098] stayed unresolved (0x7f4209887166) until S1 itself was called. The S1-then-S8 run with S1 called first (pid 32690) mirrors this.

LD_BIND_NOW=1 gives the same targets, resolved at load time. Load S8 then S1 (pid 32723): right after S1 loads, S1 GOT[0xa098] = 0x7fca54f31f90 (S8+0x2f90) and S1 GOT[0xa078] = 0x7fca54f313b0 (S8+0x23b0). Load S1 then S8 (pid 32745): S8 GOT[0x9098] = 0x7f0275088a10 (S1+0x3a10) and S8 GOT[0x9078] = 0x7f02750873b0 (S1+0x23b0). Isolated runs in either mode resolve to their own DSO: S8 slots to S8+0x2f90 and S8+0x23b0, S1 slots to S1+0x3a10 and S1+0x23b0.

Entry-DSO check. dlsym(dlopen(path, RTLD_NOLOAD|RTLD_LAZY), "run_main_graph_model") always returns the object's own entry: S1 base+0x3a70 and S8 base+0x2ff0, equal to st_value, in every order. dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, ...) returns the first-loaded object's entry. So only a global-scope lookup would pick the wrong entry, and the runtime does not use one. The lazy GOT transitions (only the called object's ciface slot gets resolved) independently confirm that the requested object's own entry and PLT executed.

Execution-level trap matrix with no tracer and no GOT reading (B_tracerfree/trap_matrix.py, results in trap_matrix.json). I made scratch copies of S8 and S1 with ud2 patched at the start of the entry (E), ciface (C) or main_graph (M), and ran 48 fresh plain processes: 6 poisoned variants x 2 load orders x 2 call targets x {lazy, LD_BIND_NOW=1}. A poisoned entry traps only when that artifact is the one called. A poisoned ciface or main_graph traps whenever the poisoned copy is loaded first, whichever artifact is called (SIGILL, rc=-4). When the poisoned copy is loaded second it never traps, and output is EXACT even when the poisoned artifact itself is called. All 48 runs match claim (B). The model 'each call runs its own code' matches only 32 of 48; all 16 runs that separate the two models side with (B).

Cross-check with the claimed evidence. In C81-1, gdb records the S1 entry at 0x3a70, then the S8 wrapper at 0x2f90, then S8 compute at 0x23b0. In C18-8 it records the S8 entry at 0x2ff0, the S1 wrapper at 0x3a10 and S1 compute at 0x23b0. The lazy LD_DEBUG logs bind the later object's _mlir_ciface reference to the first object and never bind the later object's main_graph_model. These all match the tracer-free GOT and trap results exactly.
weaknesses_found: Neither gdb/ptrace nor LD_DEBUG produced the result. The same binding appears in plain processes with TracerPid=0 and no LD_* variables, under both lazy and LD_BIND_NOW=1 binding, and in an execution-level trap test that needs no tracer.

The mechanism is narrower than 'the later artifact runs the earlier artifact's code'. The later artifact's own entry (run_main_graph_model) runs. The misbinding happens at its PLT call to _mlir_ciface_main_graph_model, which resolves to the first-loaded object. That wrapper then calls main_graph through the first object's own GOT. The later object's main_graph_model GOT slot is never used; under lazy binding it stays unresolved. The claimed table's entry=own / wrapper=other / compute=other rows already say this, so this is a precision note, not a contradiction.

Output equality cannot tell the arms apart: S8 and S1 produce the identical exact permutation. The table's exact_permutation check is therefore not identity evidence. Identity rests only on the tracer, GOT and trap evidence.

Scope: I checked independently only the two-library S8/S1 untagged pair at K, L=64. The 3-library SCAN-S8-S1-AA case and the CAA A/A case were not re-derived. The FIRST-loaded rule is standard glibc global-scope search order, and my dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT) results agree with it.

My entry check calls dlsym on a handle from dlopen(RTLD_NOLOAD), not the session's stored handle. glibc returns the same link_map for the same file, and the entry-level ud2 trap independently confirms that the requested object's own entry executes.

Process note: e1_verify/ is shared with concurrent verifiers. My first Write overwrote e1_verify/got_probe.py, which another agent's run_got.py references; that agent's runs had already finished at 01:49. All my later files are under e1_verify/B_tracerfree/. Nothing under /home/user/Shape-Perf or /home/user/work was modified: sha256 of both originals is unchanged, and the ud2 patches were applied to copies in scratch only.

results.claim: (A) Untagged: a process that loads only one artifact (S1 alone, or S8 alone) runs that artifact's own compute code. (C) With distinct tags (alpha/bravo), every call runs its own compute code in every load order and call order; loading two artifacts with the same tag mis-binds again.
independent_checks: Artifact identity: all 6 model.so files (S8, S1, S8_alpha, S1_bravo, S8_bravo, S1_alpha) have the sha256 given in identity_table.json (for example S8a c18036e3..., S1b 227c7cd9...).

Runtime source at 1e017c9f, src/Runtime/ExecutionSession.cpp: loads with dlopen(path, RTLD_LAZY|RTLD_GLOBAL). An empty tag becomes the lowercased file basename ('model'). The entry is found with dlsym(handle, 'run_main_graph_' + tag). None of the models has DT_FLAGS BIND_NOW.

readelf --dyn-syms, S8_alpha (S1_bravo is analogous): tag-suffixed symbols are main_graph_alpha 0x23b0 (size 3026), _mlir_ciface_main_graph_alpha 0x2f90, run_main_graph_alpha 0x2ff0, plus omQueryEntryPoints/omInputSignature/omOutputSignature/omCompilationInfo_alpha and _entry_point_*_alpha. For S1_bravo: main_graph_bravo 0x23b0 (size 5728), ciface 0x3a10, run 0x3a70.

Symbols still shared (untagged) in every tagged build: run_main_graph (a 5-byte jmp to run_main_graph_<tag>@plt), omQueryEntryPoints, omInputSignature, omOutputSignature, omCompilationInfo, all omTensor*/omTensorList* helpers, om_f16/f32/bf16 conversions, __truncsfhf2/__extendhfsf2/__gnu_*, OMInstrumentPoint, omInstrumentPrint, getInstrumentFile, OM_DATA_TYPE_SIZE, OM_DATA_TYPE_NAME, timing_nest_level, bufferIndex, startReportPrinted.

readelf -rW, relocations against symbols the model itself defines: 18 JUMP_SLOTs (ciface, main_graph_<tag>, run_main_graph_<tag>, getInstrumentFile, 12 omTensor*, om_f16_to_f32, om_f32_to_f16) and 10 GLOB_DATs (OM_DATA_TYPE_NAME/SIZE, bufferIndex, startReportPrinted, 6x _entry_point_*_<tag>). The slots that matter are S8a ciface at 0x9018 and main_graph_alpha at 0x9148; S1b main_graph_bravo at 0xa070 and ciface at 0xa090.

objdump of the compute functions: main_graph_alpha (S8a) contains exactly one call, '23bf: call 21d0 <malloc@plt>'; main_graph_bravo (S1b) likewise, '23c3: call 21d0 <malloc@plt>'. Neither has indirect call/jmp or a jump leaving the function. Their rip-relative operands point only into the model's own .rodata (0x6000-0x6640 in S8a, 0x7000-0x7120 in S1b), never into .got or .got.plt. The untagged S8/S1 main_graph_model has the same single malloc@plt call. The ciface's only call is main_graph_<tag>@plt (S8a at 2fa4 to 22c0, S1b at 3a24 to 2110). So no shared model symbol is reachable from main_graph_<tag>. The shared omTensor* helpers (13 PLT calls) are reached only from run_main_graph_<tag>.

Tracer-free GOT probe (no gdb, no LD_DEBUG, no shapeperf code). Each scenario ran in a fresh process: PyRuntime OMExecutionSession, then in-process ctypes reads of each GOT slot at l_addr + reloc offset, where l_addr came from /proc/self/maps and was cross-checked against link_map l_addr/l_name. Each address was mapped to its DSO and dynsym name, and the bytes at the resolved compute address were hashed. In total: 14 scenarios under both default lazy binding and LD_BIND_NOW=1, plus 5 extra lazy scenarios, giving 33 processes and 86 calls. All 86 outputs equal expected.npy exactly.

Claim (A). ISO_S1 (lazy, pid 563, base 0x7f010c52e000): after load, both slots held S1's own .plt stub+6 (unresolved). After the calls, the S1 ciface slot pointed to S1+0x3a10 _mlir_ciface_main_graph_model and the S1 main_graph slot to S1+0x23b0 main_graph_model. The in-memory hash was 7f634c25..., equal to the table's S1 value. ISO_S8: S8+0x2f90, then S8+0x23b0, hash 49916aec... Every other model-defined slot resolved inside the same DSO. LD_BIND_NOW gave the same result.

Claim (C), distinct tags: T_L8a1b_C8a, T_L8a1b_C1b, T_L1b8a_C8a, T_L1b8a_C1b, T_SEQ_8a_1b and T_SEQ_1b_8a, under both lazy and bind-now. For every call, the entry found by dlsym(handle), the ciface slot and the main_graph slot all resolve in the requested DSO: S8a goes to S8a+0x2f90 then S8a+0x23b0 (hash 7a2b158c...), and S1b goes to S1b+0x3a10 then S1b+0x23b0 (hash 807e81de...). Extra lazy runs gave the same result for S8b+S1a and S8a+S8b in both load orders.

Claim (C), same tag: in SAME_L8a1a_C1a and SAME_L8a1a_C8a, S1a's ciface slot pointed to S8a+0x2f90 and then S8a main_graph_alpha+0x23b0 (hash 7a2b...), whichever was called first. Under lazy binding, S1a's own main_graph_alpha slot stayed at its .plt stub (0x22c6), meaning S1a's compute was never reached. In SAME_L1a8a_*, S8a's ciface pointed to S1a+0x3a10 and then S1a+0x23b0. The pair S1b+S8b (both tagged bravo) behaved the same way: the S8b call ran S1b's compute. Bind-now gave the same result.

Positive control (untagged co-load, showing the method can detect mis-binding): in CTRL_L81_C1, S1's ciface slot pointed to S8+0x2f90 and then S8 main_graph_model. In CTRL_L18_C8, S8's ciface pointed to S1+0x3a10 and then S1. This matches claim (B).
Across all runs, the in-memory hash of every executed compute function equals the table's compute_function_sha256 for that arm (S8 4991..., S1 7f63..., S8a/S8b 7a2b..., S1a/S1b 807e...).
weaknesses_found: Claim (C) holds for the compute code (ciface and main_graph_<tag>), but not for the whole call path. With distinct tags co-loaded, the later-loaded model's untagged slots still bind to the first-loaded model. Under lazy binding these are 11 omTensor* JUMP_SLOTs, for example T_L8a1b_C1b: S1b.omTensorGetDataPtr points to S8a+0x37d0. The GLOB_DATs OM_DATA_TYPE_SIZE (to S8a+0x6d40), OM_DATA_TYPE_NAME, bufferIndex and startReportPrinted do the same. Under LD_BIND_NOW, getInstrumentFile, omTensorDestroy, om_f16_to_f32 and om_f32_to_f16 also move. So the entry wrapper run_main_graph_<tag> runs the other model's tensor-helper copies. This is harmless for compute identity, but 'every call runs its own code' should be worded as 'its own compute code'.

Tagging did not remove all shared exports. run_main_graph, omQueryEntryPoints, omInputSignature, omOutputSignature and omCompilationInfo are still exported without a tag. The untagged run_main_graph jumps through run_main_graph_<tag>@plt, which is safe only while tags differ. A consumer that uses tag='NONE' or the untagged entry names depends on how dlsym and global-scope lookup behave, and this was not tested.

The output check cannot tell the arms apart: S8 and S1 both produce the exact permutation, and all 86 calls, including the mis-bound ones, matched expected.npy exactly. Identity rests entirely on DSO address mapping and GOT or trace evidence.

The compute-byte hash cannot separate builds that share a policy but differ in tag: S8a and S8b are both 7a2b..., and S1a and S1b are both 807e.... Only the DSO that contains the address separates them. The table's executed_bytes_match_arms lists a single arm only because it compares within one tag.

Scope: covers only the K-type transpose at L=64, PyRuntime at 1e017c9f, glibc 2.39 on x86_64, and a development container. Other ops, cells, and loaders such as ctypes, ORT or a C++ host were not checked.

A sibling verifier writes to the same scratch directory, e1_verify/, and overwrote a file I had written (got_probe.py). All of my files are in e1_verify/AC_gotcheck/; the other files in e1_verify/ belong to the sibling.

defects.defect: The co-loading guard fails open when a library yields an empty model-symbol set. It never checks that each library exports at least one model symbol. MODEL_SYMBOL_RE requires a '_<tag>' suffix, so libraries built with ONNX-MLIR '--tag=NONE' are missed: that option is supported (CompilerUtils.cpp:258, ExecutionSession.cpp:118) and makes the libraries export plain main_graph, _mlir_ciface_main_graph and run_main_graph. elfinfo also reads symbols only through section headers, so a .so with e_shnum=0 (section headers stripped) has no dynsym entries either. In both cases assert_no_shared_model_symbols passes, and paired.py:109 lets subgraph_pair_worker co-load libraries that do mis-bind.
defects.failure_scenario: Both cases reproduced in scratchpad/e1_verify. (1) none/: two libraries with untagged main_graph, _mlir_ciface_main_graph and run_main_graph, returning 8 and 1. model_symbols() returns set(), the guard passes, and after RTLD_GLOBAL co-loading B's entry returns 8 (A's compute). (2) nosh/: the test fixture with tag 'model', put through llvm-objcopy --strip-sections. model_symbols() returns set() (the unstripped file gives {main_graph_model, run_main_graph_model}), the guard passes, and B's run_main_graph_model returns 8. No current artifact is in either state, so claims A-C are not affected.

defects.defect: If the worker running under gdb does not finish (a Python exception, a crash, or gdb unable to ptrace), calls_gdb.jsonl is never written, because it is written only at the end of the worker. analyse_case then silently returns zero rows instead of 'unresolved' rows. runs['gdb']['returncode'] is recorded but never consulted, so the case disappears from rows and from verdict_counts.
defects.failure_scenario: Simulated on a copy of identity_orig/C81-1 with calls_gdb.jsonl deleted: analyse_case returns rows=[] and verdict_counts would show 0 unresolved. It does not change the current tables: all 29 cases are complete (36 orig and 58 tagged rows, each with exactly entry/wrapper/compute hits per call).

defects.defect: The LD_DEBUG cross-check is skipped without any trace when no binding line is parsed (lazy is None). No reason is added and the verdict stays verified_own or verified_other. The LD runs' return codes are also ignored. A glibc format change, a mismatch between the dlopen path string and the arm path in the substring filter, or a crashed LD run all silently remove the corroboration.
defects.failure_scenario: Simulated on a copy of C81-1 with both ld_bindings files emptied: the same 4 verdicts (verified_other/verified_own) come back with wrapper_reference_of_requested_bound_to=None and no reason. It does not change the current tables: every row in both tables has non-null lazy and bindnow bindings that agree with gdb.

defects.defect: The tests would pass with parts of the mechanism or verifier broken. test_rtld_global_distinct_tags_run_own_compute does not have the _calls_through_plt precondition that the same-tag test has (line 69). With a compiler that binds main_graph_* locally, the same-tag test is skipped while the distinct-tag test passes vacuously, so it cannot tell 'distinct tags fixed it' from 'interposition impossible'. The real-artifact tests cover only the happy path: no test checks that analyse_case gives 'unresolved' for a hit-count mismatch, a byte mismatch or a missing calls log, and none checks the guard's fail-open on an empty symbol set.
defects.failure_scenario: Deleting the count check at verify_execution_identity.py:205-206, or the empty-rows handling, still passes all 8 tests, because the real evidence is consistent. On a clang toolchain without PLT calls, test 1 skips and test 2 still passes. In this container gcc emits PLT calls, so test 1 ran and passed (8 passed, none skipped).

checked_ok: Verdict: claims (A), (B) and (C) survive. I checked them without gdb and without shapeperf code (scratchpad/e1_verify/got_probe.py, run_probe.py, run_probe_aa.py). In fresh processes using OMExecutionSession, after the calls I read each loaded model's .got.plt slots for _mlir_ciface_main_graph_<tag> and main_graph_<tag> and mapped them to DSOs by base address plus st_value.

Results of that check: I8 and I1 run their own code. C81-1, C81-8 and SEQ81 run S1 through S8's wrapper and compute. C18-8, C18-1, SEQ18 and load1-call1-load8-call8 run S8 through S1's. SCAN (S8,S1,AA) runs S1 and AA through S8. CAA runs AA through S8, and CAA-rev runs S8 through AA. All distinct-tag cases (C8a1b, C1b8a, C8b1a, C1a8b, SEQ8a1b, SEQ1b8a, CAA-8a8b) run their own code. SAMETAG-8a1a runs S1a through S8a, and SAMETAG-1a8a runs S8a through S1a. All outputs were exact.

gdb evidence is consistent in both tables. For every case, gdb_hits.jsonl is exactly the entry, wrapper, compute sequence once per call, with consecutive seq, a single pid, no tracer_error, and module_relative_start == elf_symbol_value on every hit. Row counts (36 orig, 58 tagged) equal the call counts. In every row the LD_DEBUG lazy and bindnow wrapper binding is non-null and agrees with the gdb wrapper DSO.
Hit-to-call grouping is conservative. Simulating a missing first entry hit made all 4 rows of C81-1 unresolved. Extra or missing wrapper/compute hits and byte mismatches also lead to unresolved.

Compute identity is fully captured by the bytes of main_graph_<tag>. Disassembly shows main_graph_* calls only malloc@plt, the wrapper calls main_graph_<tag>@plt, and the entry calls wrapper@plt plus omTensor* runtime helpers.

Byte-identical copies are handled correctly. S8 and AA (sha 49916aec...) and S8a and S8b (7a2b158c...) have identical compute bytes, so for those rows the verdict rests on gdb.solib_name, which is address-based, and a note is attached. The GOT probe confirms the path-based attributions independently (CAA: AA runs S8's code; CAA-8a8b: each runs its own).

elfinfo struct layouts and field indices are correct for EHDR, PHDR, SHDR and SYM. vaddr_to_offset uses p_filesz. Executed memory bytes match the file bytes: the PIC text has no text relocations, and gdb shadows its breakpoints.

Pinned runtime 1e017c9: ExecutionSession.cpp:132 opens the model with dlopen(RTLD_LAZY|RTLD_GLOBAL), and line 247 finds the entry with dlsym on the model's own handle. The derived tag is the lower-cased file stem, which matches _names() ('model').

The paired.py:109 guard runs before affinity and before any load, and covers every loaded arm, including arms that are not timed. It refuses S8/S1 untagged and the AA byte copy, accepts distinct tags, and correctly ignores the untagged run_main_graph/omQueryEntryPoints/omInputSignature/omOutputSignature/omCompilationInfo symbols that every library exports.

tests/test_loader_identity.py: 8 passed and none skipped, including the real-artifact gdb tests. The same-tag fixture really calls through the PLT here. Rule note: the test run may have refreshed git-ignored __pycache__ files under the repo; all later checks used PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, and no tracked file changed.
